utterances.text: So I take it from that answer, witness, that you didn't feel it was necessary to review the specific evidence put before the Trial Chamber relating to the specific scheduled sniping and shelling incidents. Is that what you're telling us?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. You didn't understand me very well. I have studied all the testimony heard here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You just said, "As for specific incidents, you had testimony on that, you had experts, and there was no reason for me to study them in particular, in addition to what they said here and what they have prepared for this."

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But please read the sentence before that. I said that I have studied all that and that I have heard all the testimony, but I did not make a detailed investigation and research into each and every incident because that's not my role here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, can you point us to any citation or reference in your report to the actual testimony or evidence relating to any of the specific victims of a scheduled sniping or shelling incident?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In a footnote I wrote that sniping incidents are a matter that needs to be investigated by an expert. A military expert cannot analyse every detail separately because my report would then be 10.000 pages long.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you have written in your report and testified here today that you reached the conclusion that the accused was not guilty with respect to the sniping and shelling charges. How is it possible for you to reach that conclusion unless you had recourse to the evidence with respect to those incidents on the particular day and time that the incidents allegedly occurred?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. It's a tendentious question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The objection is denied by a majority decision, Judge Nieto-Navia dissenting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, would you like me to repeat the question?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You have written in your report and testified here today that you reached the conclusion that the accused was not guilty with respect to the sniping and shelling charges. How is it possible for you to reach that conclusion unless you had recourse to the evidence with respect to those incidents on the particular day and time that the incidents allegedly occurred?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: First of all, I said that I have studied all the incidents that are alleged in the indictment, but I didn't go to the spot where it happened as an expert for sniping to study that myself. I studied other people's analyses. I don't see what else I could have done.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I'm not asking you if you conducted an investigation. I'm simply asking you where in your report you specify which evidence regarding the specific incidents that you relied upon, whether it was witness testimony, victim testimony, medical records, et cetera. Where in your report do you indicate the material you relied on with respect to the specific scheduled sniping and shelling incidents?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, insofar as the witness does not listen to Falstaff's language, he only hears the interpretation, it would be good for the Prosecutor to clarify his question, as well as his previous question, because he's now talking about a different question, not the one he asked before that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the question I asked before that was answered, and then I moved on to another question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, I would agree. Because when Mr. Mundis repeated the question, he literally repeated that question. The question was then answered, and then the next question started with: "Witness, I'm not asking you if you --" so referring to --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. But then, Mr. Mundis, you continued: "I'm simply asking you." And that was not a repetition of your previous. So you put a question to the witness, and we had an objection. Then you repeated the same question and you got an answer, which in your view was not an answer to the question. And then you said "I'm simply asking you," and then the question that follows is not exactly the same as you put before to the witness. So if you would please clarify that, we'll avoid whatever confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, are there any references in your report to the testimony of victims or witnesses to the scheduled sniping and shelling incidents?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: There is shelling -- we're talking about the football match in Dobrinja, about Mahala, about the Ciglane shelling. As for sniping, I viewed it as a general problem, not as incidents. I bore in mind that the Defence and the Prosecution both have experts especially for that, and I didn't view my role as involving the review of specific sniping incidents. I viewed sniping and treated it as a military problem, and that's what I wrote about in my statement. As far as this is concerned, I dealt with it in detail and my report contains a particular chapter on this issue --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: -- With references to documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With respect to the Ciglane shelling, what expert report did you review concerning that incident?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I dealt with Ciglane in my conclusion number 33 of the report, saying that in some of the accompanying documents it was said that Ciglane neighbourhood suffered because fire was returned by the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. That is in conclusion number 33 in my report.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, the question was: You've told us that you have reviewed --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour. The first of the questions was not which expert he had or which expert report he read but if he read any expert report referring to Ciglane. I am reminding you that the witness is listening to interpretation and that the appropriate linguistic and semantic distance needs to be taken into account.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Was there any confusion? Did you review any expert report on Ciglane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I reviewed a sea of material about shelling, and as far as I can remember now I first studied all of that and then the Defence team, as I could conclude, this incident with Ciglane was written off in the indictment and I didn't deal with it any more. But I mentioned this in my report in order to illustrate how certain neighbourhoods come to suffer consequences because fire is opened from them against the Sarajevo Romanija Corps and when fire is returned, these neighbourhoods suffer. And I illustrated this using the example of Ciglane. That's all there is to it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are you able to repeat what I asked you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You asked me whether I have studied material about the Ciglane incident.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I asked whether you studied an expert report on Ciglane. Did you study any expert report on Ciglane?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me turn back to the map D1913 that you have before you. Witness, there's no date or range of dates or scale indicated on that map, is there?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The map that you produced, D1913, does it have a date on it, indicating the date of the information that's on that map?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mean the date when they happened or when -- the date when I put them? I don't understand you again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: You reviewed about 25 --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'll clarify the question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Is it -- would that help you out, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, if the question would be clarified?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Are we talking about this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We're talking about D1913, with the numerous coloured circle that is the witness produced.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's the map that is in front of the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately I did not number it myself, but is it this map?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could I just check the witness's map, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honour, if Mr. Piletta-Zanin is going to point out that the map actually has a date by the company that produced the map, that's not the issue.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That's not the issue. Is that the problem you have, Mr. Piletta-Zanin?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's -- when we are talking about maps, one date -- Okay. Please tell us what the problem is.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I thought -- but it just disappeared from my screen because I'm trying to focus as much as I can. In the question put by Mr. Mundis, it is asserted that there is no scale on this map. However, I can read here, under "D," in quadrant D, 13 -- something that looks like a scale.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Map you're using that --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's the question I was asking, if we're talking about the same map. Here down below. It may be that this was erased during printing --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Could I see both maps -- I'd like to see the maps so that we see whether we're talking about the same map or not.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It may be that working with a document used for preparations --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could I please have both maps.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, since I have only that copy, it may be that it's not completely identical. It's a working document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, when we are talking about maps, we are talking about the maps as they get numbers, that's D1913 and that should be the same as the map you're referring to. Would you please refrain from referring to maps that are not produced and are different --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... And would you please be more restrictive in your objections, because this is not a way to interfere in the --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you've told us that this map was created on the basis of about 25 documents which were then admitted into evidence or tendered into evidence under Defence number 1915. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: 24. I'm sorry, that's right. Because one of them I think you said was a --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: But you have cardinal numbers from 1 to 25, and 16 is missing, number 16 is missing, so we have 25 numbers and only 24 documents.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Now, those documents, those 24 documents, were the primary sources for the information that you've placed on map D1913; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The 24 documents have a wide range of dates; isn't that right? Or were all of those 24 documents produced on the same day?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, they were not produced on the same day, but they all referred to the units which were located in the area of responsibility in question throughout the war. So the timing absolutely does not affect the data about the accuracy of targets within the city.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, witness, wouldn't it be correct, however, that -- to state that this map represents an accumulation of information covering the dates or the range of dates that the underlying documents reflect?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: In replying to questions in chief, I talked about this map. I said it was produced based on data collected from various documents, documents of different types and provenance to illustrate the position that Sarajevo held an entire armed corps, from 10 to 15 brigades, and that's what I have shown here in this graph.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, my question --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: And that is the purport of this map. It is not the purpose of the map for every little circle to bear a date, although every little circle does bear a date, indicating which target it refers to, which location, and which date. We can easily establish that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's what my question goes to, witness. The fact of the matter is that not all of these targets were at the locations marked on this map on the same day. The map was --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, not on the same day.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: So this map represents an accumulation based on the 24 documents that you produced. You went through the documents, and if on a given day a unit was at a specific location, you marked that on the map.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: You seem to be using the term "accumulation" in a context in which I don't think you should be using it. "Accumulation" doesn't mean that I'm showing several targets than actually existed based on various documents. A brigade can only have one firing group. In this 102nd Brigade, there is only one firing group, not two. It is only drawn in to show that on this 1st February of 1994 it was located here. I didn't draw two of them.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I understand, witness.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So you don't use the term "accumulation" meaning that there was an accumulation of targets.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'm not trying to suggest that there was. What I'm trying to suggest is that the circles which you drew on these maps came from documents with a wide range of dates, so that this map does not produce a picture of the city of Sarajevo on any given date but, rather, reflects the placement of these targets on particular dates as reflected in the 24 documents.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are only selected documents concerning brigades that were permanently located in these locations. In terms of territory covered, there was absolutely no dynamics. It is here, whether it's called the 3rd or the 102nd, until March 1993, it was called 3rd and from then on it was called 102nd Motorised Brigade. But they were there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Both before and after March 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Due to time constraints, witness, I'm sorry, but I need to cut you off. The question - I'll repeat it if you'd like me to - but the question goes to the dates that the symbols on the map refer to. My question simply is: Does the map reflect the situation on one day or does the information reflected on the map represent information that you obtained on a variety of dates, as reflected in the 24 documents?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This map provides a rough image of the military targets in Sarajevo while General Galic had a mandate, during his term of office. That was the purpose of this map. And I'd like to repeat this. It's an illustration. It doesn't include everything, because all the targets couldn't be represented, because they're nothing -- it wouldn't be possible to see anything in the city given the numerous targets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: General Radinovic, there seems to be a kind of a Babelonic situation where the Prosecution asks you repeatedly a question and you repeatedly are explaining something which is not directly related to the question. Do I understand your testimony well that this map does not reflect all military positions but only a selection?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do I understand you well that the markings you made were on the basis of documents which bear a different date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: And that, therefore, this map reflects the positions, at least on those dates and not necessarily all of them on one date?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's true that it doesn't reflect the positions on just one date, but it reflects the positions in that area. And I recorded those positions on that date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. It's perfectly clear. Please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you told us a few days ago that the Sarajevo Romanija Corps or Republika Srpska had six goals and that the destruction of Sarajevo was not one of those goals. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I think you also told us that you had never seen any SRK documents indicating that the destruction of Sarajevo was a goal of either Republika Srpska or the Sarajevo Romanija Corps. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: With the assistance of the usher, I would ask that the -- that this document be shown to the witness. While this document is being circulated:

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, have you seen any documents indicating -- as part of your review, any documents indicating that the destruction of Sarajevo was a goal of the Republika Srpska?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I haven't seen a single document that would show that the destruction of Sarajevo was one of Republika Srpska's objectives. On the contrary: At its assembly session, Republika Srpska in the constitution, in Article 4 of its constitution, mentioned Sarajevo as its capital and would therefore be mad if one of its objectives was to destroy its capital.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, the document you have before you now on the upper right has a stamp of the command of the 1st Partisan Brigade. Have you seen this document before?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Was this one of the 130 -- approximately 130 documents that was attached to and filed with your report?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you could turn to the fourth page of that document in both -- for the benefit of the Chamber, the fourth page of the English version as well. Can you tell us who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some captain first class Viktor Momcilo [as interpreted]. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, this document purports to be minutes of a meeting. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it seems to have that form, the form of minutes of a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And Captain Momcilo took the minutes of this meeting; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Or rather, if it's authentic, yes, he did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the form, it seems to be the minutes of a meeting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And based on the stamp that you see on the upper right of the first page of this document, this document was received by the 1st Partisan Brigade; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I apologise. I just wanted to point out that the Defence has objected. It contests the authenticity of this document and we have said why we contest its authenticity, as was requested by the Trial Chamber.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask this be done in the absence of the witness, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. May I ask you, General Radinovic, to leave the courtroom for a while.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I would just like to draw your attention to the fact that this document -- I think the footnote is 83 and it was part of the expert report of Robert Donia's. And on that occasion the Defence contested the authenticity of the document. The Trial Chamber decided to have it admitted as part of the expert report and then we heard Mrs. Jelena Guskova, an expert for the Defence, and the Prosecution presented two sources for this document then, and we still don't know what the source of this document is. Now the Prosecution is showing a document that is part of footnote 83, and when Mrs. Guskova was heard, we had this document without a single page and the Defence was ordered by the Trial Chamber with regard to this document that has all the pages and with regard to the document that doesn't have one page, the Defence was ordered to explain what its objections were, and the Defence submitted a submission in which it explained why it was contesting the authenticity of this document. First of all, we have never seen the original of this document. We don't know what the source of this document is. Here it says the "1st Partisan Brigade," which is also contested, which is also in dispute. And for these reasons, the Defence objects to showing this document in that -- to showing this document to the witness so that he could interpret it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. One question, Ms. Pilipovic: I do understand from the answer to one of the questions that this document was attached to the report of the expert.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, it wasn't attached to the expert report. It was only analysed in the expert report. But it wasn't attached as evidence. It was only analysed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The question was put to the witness: "Was this one of the 130 -- approximately 130 documents that was attached to and filed with your report?" And the witness said: "Yes, I think so." But of course this leaves some reason for doubt. Ms. --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think that there was a misunderstanding between the expert and the question put by my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then at least this should be clarified, whenever the witness returns. But -- Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I will endeavour to double-check whether this was in fact attached to his report. He certainly, as Ms. Pilipovic indicates, makes reference to the document in his report, and the witness himself indicated that he thinks it was probably attached to his report. The point is, Mr. President, that this witness has said he's never seen a document that goes to the destruction of the city of Sarajevo. This document, which he has in fact seen, there is reference to that in this document. So once --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: It's not on my mind at this very moment where exactly it is. If the parties could provide the Chamber --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, in the English version, it would be on the third page, about a third of the way down under number 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just see.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Your Honour. On page 44 in the Serbian version all other interpretations of that target or those targets.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Are we now correcting the transcript or ...?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me just confer with my colleague.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I was -- we were dealing with --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We're discussing the document, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2 of the document, yes. I now understand what my colleague is referring to on page 3. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, you said reference was made in number 5 -- oh, in that document. There seems to be a lot of confusion. I was trying to find the place where in the report of the expert we'd find reference to this document just --

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Item 102. That would be footnote 50, see the minutes of the meeting with municipality presidents.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: What I find in footnote 48 is a document which is not, as far as I remember, unrelated to this document but it's not the same document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if you would look at footnote number 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 50, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The ERN numbers match, with respect to the B/C/S version of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 50.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: 50. Now it's clear to me, "the transcript of the meeting with the presidents of the municipalities". Let me just see in the text whether there's any reservation as to the authenticity of this document. The document is referred to by the expert, so -- we have a corresponding ERN number and we have a four-page document, and that was a problem in the past. Ms. Pilipovic, if an expert refers to a certain document and if he has explained to us that he received documents from the Defence and if he makes no reservation as far as the authenticity is concerned, what would be the reason to forbid the Prosecution to show that document? I mean, it's part of his report, isn't it?

utterances.speaker: MS. PILIPOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I just wanted to point out that there is such an objection. I wanted to inform the Trial Chamber of the position of the Defence. That was why I stood up and made this comment with regard to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, let's then proceed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Judge Nieto-Navia has a question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, you were referring to page 3 of the English transcript, number 5, and I think that was the line of your questioning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That would be where I would take the witness to, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Okay. My question is the following: It says, at least in the document that I have, "double-underlined in the original." Do you agree with that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes, it does, Your Honour. And --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: Well, now you can go to page 3 of the B/C/S version and look at number 5.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And there is no double-underlining.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE NIETO-NAVIA
utterances.text: The problem is that sometimes the documents of the Prosecutor bring comments included, like certain Bibles. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I would like to thank Judge Nieto-Navia for the acuity he has brought to bear on the matter, and I think I understand why the error lies. You remember that there are two documents: One in reference to page 2 that we examined with our Russian expert, I think, and the other is this entire document. And I think that what has happened is that we have been given a draft translation that concerns another document. But as the other document is not exactly identical, this is why this problem has arisen. So couldn't we ask the Prosecution to make a distinction, a clear distinction, and to have a translation for each document so that we can in a certain sense find our bearings. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. In order to prevent a repetition of what happened before, that is, to call the witness in again and then immediately adjourn, the Chamber would like to adjourn for 20 minutes. And perhaps in the meantime the Prosecution could provide a clean translation of this document without the issue just raised by Judge Nieto-Navia. If there's any other part of the translation that should be reviewed and if one of the parties notices that there is some incorrect part in the translation, the party should either correct or inform the other party that this does exist.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Ierace.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Just before we adjourn --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: -- Might I say a few words very quickly. Mr. President, I've spoken to Mr. Piletta-Zanin this morning in relation to the Gray tape issue. I understand that he has some information. He's told me what it is. I wonder, since the witness is -- it happens that the witness is not present at the moment and we're about to adjourn, if this would be a convenient time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, if there's anything that -- well, first of all, perhaps we should convey the message to the witness that we'll adjourn for 20 to 25 minutes so that he doesn't have to wait for us to return. And if there's anything that should be said in the absence of the witness, Mr. Piletta-Zanin, perhaps this would be an appropriate moment to do so.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, Mr. President. I did speak to Mr. Ierace this morning, and I informed him of certain situations. I told him that there was no need to bother the Trial Chamber for the moment with these matters, and he didn't take that into account, and I told him that I would provide him with all the information I could provide him with as soon as I have this information. I'd be glad to expose the matter to the Trial Chamber, but it would waste time. But if Mr. Ierace is impatient, I think that by tomorrow he will know everything about everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: The situation where the Prosecution and Defence have very different accounts of private meetings continues. I will say this, and perhaps Mr. Piletta-Zanin can confirm or deny it that he told me this morning that the fourth tape has been checked, the segment is not on it, they concede that there was a fifth tape and they are now searching for it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I said a number of things. I said that we spent quite a lot of time on reviewing all these tapes. The quality was terrible, and it's quite likely that the segment sought for wasn't there. But as the images were not very good, it's difficult to be certain. So there is probably a fifth tape. As I said, we are looking for this phantom tape. And as soon as we find it, the Prosecution will be informed of the fact and will be provided with the original, such as we received it at the time. But again, this is a hypothesis because we have to check all of this.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The -- Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, prior to us breaking, if I could get some indication from the Chamber as to how much time I have remaining, that would be very helpful.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I'm afraid that I would need to do some calculations on that because the cross-examination could not proceed as smoothly as the examination-in-chief.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps so that I could organise over the break, is the Chamber anticipating that I would be required to finish today, or will I have a little bit of time tomorrow? That would at least help for purposes of planning over the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Let me just try to calculate. But I am doing it now by heart. Yesterday I think the Prosecution took -- yes. I do understand that the Prosecution has used three hours and twenty minutes, today included. So if we would now adjourn, we would have one hour left. That would bring us to four hours and 20 minutes. And since the Defence took five hours, that would leave us with some time tomorrow. I'm not sure. I have to check with the registrar to what extent interruptions have been taken into account. But certainly there will be a little time tomorrow.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's sufficient. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We'll adjourn --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, I'm sorry. But with regard to this matter, Defence counsel thinks that if time has been wasted, this is because of the Prosecution who wanted to ask certain questions that were subjective: For example, what the responsibility, if any, of General Galic was. We have wasted this time, but this time has to be taken into account because this isn't due to the Defence. I committed one error, I think, with regard to a map, but I think everything else was due to the Prosecution. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll adjourn until quarter to 1.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. I do have corrected versions of the English translation of the document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Would you then please use that version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I would ask that you please go to the third page of the document that's now before you. This document, as we've previously addressed, concerns notes taken on 14 May 1992 at a meeting, and it appears as though the notetaker was Captain Momcilo; is that right?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's what I said.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If you'd go to, please, page 3 of this document and look at what's indicated on the document under the number 5, approximately one-third of the way down the document. Do you see what I'm referring to?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That makes reference to the destruction of Sarajevo, does it not?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It says: "The President of Mrkonjic Grad municipality," not General Galic. In fact, the notetaker says this was said by the president of the municipality of Mrkonjic Grad.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please read out precisely what it says next to the number 5 on page 3 of this document.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the proviso that these are the president of the municipality. The president of Sanski Most municipality, Milan Malidza, said in item 5, in fact, the notetaker records him as saying 'it was said that Sarajevo must be divided or razed to the ground." These are not Galic's words and this part is totally irrelevant.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The relevance of issues and who said what has not been at this very moment part of the question. So there's no need -- if someone would have asked you: Are these the words of General Galic? I can imagine that in interpreting this you would say no or -- well, whatever. But that has not been asked at this very moment. The only thing that has been asked you now is to read that part. So please would you listen careful to the question and answer the question. And if there's anything that should be said about it, first of all you have an opportunity to do so if later on there seems that there is confusion, and you might be re-examined by the Defence who might ask you questions about it as well. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, if you look at the bottom -- or perhaps the top of the following page, it indicates the -- what will happen at the end of the meeting or what happened at the end of the meeting. And there's a reference there to the accused. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. Could you guide me. Oh, you mean this sentence: "At the end of the meeting"?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's the sentence. Please, can you read that sentence out to us.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "At the end of the meeting, Colonel Galic proposed the following conclusions:"

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please read the first bullet under that.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "To implement the conclusions from the meeting in Banja Luka, but they have to be submitted to unit commands and municipalities." So these conclusions from the 12th of May, from the assembly meeting -- the assembly session of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina. Shall I read on?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's fine, witness. If you then turn to the first page of this document, you'll see approximately one-third of the way down the page a list of 11 individuals who were present at this meeting. Can you please read what's listed under number 1.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Meeting attended: Commander of the 30th Division, Colonel Stanislav Galic."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Is there reference there to that being the 30th Partisan Division?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And the stamp at the top of the document indicating the 1st Partisan Brigade, was that brigade a subordinate command of the 30th Partisan Division?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: To tell you the truth, I can't say at this moment. I wasn't interested in this at the time, and this is not the time that has to do with the period when General Galic was commander of the SRK and I didn't know anything about the composition of the 30th Partisan Division. I don't know whether this brigade was within the division.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: This document was received at the -- according to the stamp, was received at the 1st Partisan Brigade on 14 May 1992; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you told us earlier that among the transcripts of Prosecution interviews that you read was one of Major Indic. Do you remember that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I said, if I recollect it well now, that I studied -- in fact, heard the tapes of his testifying here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, I'm talking now about the interviews that were given by Major Indic to the Office of the Prosecutor. I can show you, sir, on page 5 of your report, paragraph 11 --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Well, that's fine. I reviewed that, but I wasn't sure that I had stated in this specific case that it was a transcript rather than a tape, but I studied his statement, not only his statement but the statements of all the members of the SRK with whom the Prosecution had talked, everything that was made available to me by the Defence team. I suppose they gave me everything.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, do you recall reading in Major Indic's statement to the investigator of the Tribunal that during that interview they played an audiotape of an intercept on 29 May 1992 in which General Mladic is heard ordering the shelling of certain parts of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Did I say that?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, no. Do you --

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was interpreted to me as if I had said that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No. Let me be absolutely clear. My question is: Do you remember reading in Major Indic's transcript that a tape was played during the interview of Major Indic, the investigator played a tape of an intercept from 29 May 1992 in which General Mladic is heard ordering shelling of certain parts of Sarajevo?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember that right now, to be quite frank. But if you gave me the transcript, I could see it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I do have copies here of the relevant portions of the interview with Major Indic. These are both in English and in B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Those can be distributed. I'll find the precise passage for the witness. Mr. President, for the benefit of the Chamber, on this copy it's beginning on page 77 at the very top. I do have a copy marked for the witness with the -- if that would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, if you look at the portion of the transcript which I gave you, you'll see the answer from Major Indic with respect to the tape.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is your question? That's Indic's answer, not mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Yes. You told us that you didn't remember that but if you saw the transcript it might help refresh your memory. Having reviewed the answer of Major Indic - and I'm not, witness, saying that you said this - but what Major Indic said with respect to an intercept of General Mladic from the 29th of May.

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can see this portion that you marked.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, have you ever heard the tape or seen the transcript of the intercept that is the subject --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that this be done in the absence of the witness, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could you escort the witness --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's what I asked.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- The witness out of the courtroom, Madam Usher.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour. We have an objection in principle concerning the exhibit that is produced by the Prosecutor, either the tape itself or the transcript of this interview. First of all - and we know to which point it is dangerous to make a connection between two cases - in this case General Mladic, if it is General Mladic, not simply a fabrication, the fact that we have several cases involved, even if we refer to the enigma case, we can mention several tapes that are appearing in an extremely favourable moment. So we actually have every reason to judge that this cannot be received as an authentic document. I know the Prosecutor will say that this is in fact a part of public law and the question whether the shelling of Sarajevo, forces of their own people, is part of that law. We contest the authenticity of this document because we don't know what are the forces that could have intercepted this conversation, and at the very outset, Your Honour, this being so, the date in question precedes by a long time the period when General Galic assumed command. It seems to be the 29th of May, 1992. Not only this concerns third persons, regardless of who they are, but the event itself is three months prior to the facts that are of interest to us. So there is no chronological coincidence and there is serious doubt as to what happened in Gorazde regarding this document. I don't think the Prosecution should be allowed to use this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: But before you answer, do you intend to produce the tape or do you just want to confront the witness with the statement of Mr. Indic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Actually, a third variation, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would intend to confront the witness with a transcript of the tape. Let me address a couple of issues prior to addressing the specific issues raised by Mr. Piletta-Zanin. First of all, the draft transcript of this intercept was disclosed to the Defence and had been on the Prosecution exhibit list. Second, the Defence and in particular this expert the Defence has put forth material which is not in evidence. They've canvassed material which is both before this Trial Chamber and material which has not been admitted into evidence. This witness purports to give definitive conclusions with respect to the allegations facing the accused. But to address specifically the issues that Mr. Piletta-Zanin has raised, the Prosecution has alleged that General Galic assumed command of a prior -- of an existing campaign. This evidence would go to demonstrate that. It's also the Prosecution argument that the extent of material prior to the indictment period was greatly expanded upon during the Defence case in chief, whereas the Prosecution led relatively limited amount of evidence to demonstrate that there was a campaign that had been in existence prior to the accused assuming command. It was, in the Prosecution's submission, the Defence case, which greatly expanded upon evidence with respect to those periods prior to the specific indictment period. We would point in particular to the evidence of Richard Gray, where there was extensive Defence evidence with respect to numerous shelling incidents and the party which was, in that witness's perspective, the party that was responsible for that. Mr. President, this would be the reasons why the Prosecution would put this material to this witness. We would propose to deal with any issues concerning authenticity in our rebuttal case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this calls for several comments. And from what they tell me in Latin it has a specific name: Qui tacet non quio consentire [phoen]. Concerning the provenance of this document, it remains a great secret. In the Serbian version, which I have in front of me, I see the place and date and there is no indication of these at all, so it's quite nebulous. We don't know where it comes from, what are the ways that conveyed this message, if it ever existed. We have no information on time. We don't know anything about the period after, and we have no corroboration of the authenticity whatsoever. Since the Prosecution says they have listened to this tape, we can't even determine the date of the interview let alone the date of the tape. We are doubly handicapped. We don't have an original with which to check. The Prosecution has to distinguish between evidence for and against, and since an element is so far removed in time it cannot prove, as they say, the existence of a campaign before General Galic assumed command. We have to take into account the alleged activities of the persons who are mentioned here, and I would say the historical character that it has in the conduct of fighting in the former Yugoslavia, referring to these persons means in a way that an oil stain is spilled in the path of the Defence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: [Previous interpretation continues] ... Yes. I was not waiting for the translation. I apologise for that. What's the purpose? Do you want to establish whether the expert explored all the potential sources or do you want to establish that a telephone conversation has taken place? What's the -- what's the purpose?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the purpose is actually both, although let me say that it's not a telephone conversation but it was a radio transmission that was captured.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But our purpose would be to establish -- the witness has told us at great length the methodology that he employed. He's told us how he's considered himself to be an independent expert and an unbiased expert. He had access -- or this Indic transcript, which he read, clearly refers to this tape. It would seem that in light of the specific allegations against this accused that that would be the type of material that an expert in his shoes, who was attempting to undertake an independent and unbiased investigation or to prepare a report, would have sought out this information. That's the first point. Let me just quickly hit two other points. First of all, this conversation, the taped intercept, is actually in the public domain, has been broadcast on television in Sarajevo, it's been -- the transcripts of this have been reproduced in at least one published book that the Prosecution is aware of. With respect to the authenticity, last week we took a 92 bis statement of the head of the ABiH intelligence at the time who personally was involved in this intercept, and that will be handed over to the Defence tomorrow. As I said, we got that last week. I should also point out that the formal translation, as well as a copy of the tape with respect to the segment that I would take the witness -- the witness to -- the transcript that I would take the witness to was disclosed to the Defence about two weeks ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, as for the source that we are now discovering, we have to be even more cautious because we know that television in general, and especially during the war, is in the power of civilian nonmilitary authorities that employ them, and this was made public only by the forces of the presidency. In fact, their radio and television. It seems this source is extremely biased and unilateral, and if we are going to base ourselves on this public source, we have to take into account that Sarajevo, which is the place where the war started, it would be very dangerous to accept this claim. The Prosecution doesn't seem to claim that other televisions, TF1, or some international televisions ever carried this claim or this conversation, in fact.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber allows the document and material related to this overheard conversation to be shown to the witness and to be -- there's nothing to be played to the witness, but only in respect of the way he uses his sources and not in order to establish through this witness whether such a telephone conversation ever took place and whether he recognises voices, et cetera, et cetera. There's no reason to believe that this expert witness could have any specific knowledge on that. So the exercise is admissible but in order to question the witness about the way he explored the sources available to him.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know very well that this is a subject that I can deal with during redirect, but General Galic asked me to intervene and I'm doing it. I think it would be a good idea to draw the witness's attention to the Serbian version as it appears in our document, namely the portion that follows, starting with the words "I heard that." We could see what actually happened, and I think this would help the witness answer.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Do we have the Serbian version of the -- we have it, yes. I see the translation is part of it. So preferably -- I take it that these are the original words used, that we rely upon that as much as possible, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I'm a bit confused. Is Mr. Piletta-Zanin referring to the Indic transcript or to the transcript of the tape?

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, obviously. I just said so. "I heard about this tape" and so on and so forth. So that is this line. You have it right in front of you, Mr. Mundis, page 116 -- sorry, 77.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So the answer is referred to the Indic interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I could just have a brief moment to confer before the witness is brought back into the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please do so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: Page 76.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, perhaps an issue of clarification from the Trial Chamber might be of assistance. I'm understanding the Chamber's ruling to be that I can put to the witness the issue of whether or not he relied or had recourse to the tape or a transcript of the intercepted tape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. And also whether, for what reason, whether he used it or whether he denied it and for what reasons. I mean, whatever in the field of the expert.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: In which case, simply for clarification, for purposes of the Defence, I have no further need to deal with the Indic transcript.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But very unfortunately we don't need it if we are going to ask questions about Mladic. Either we are going to forget the whole subject and that would be okay or we are going to deal with it fully.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Well, the Prosecution may put the questions to the witness as they want, as long as it's not to establish whether this telephone conversation took place, because I do understand that -- unless there's a specific reason why this witness would know anything about that. But not just on the basis of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, upon reflection and in light of the issue raised by the Defence, we will begin by taking the witness to page 76 of the Indic transcript, beginning with that portion at the top of that page indicating a tape recording, through pages 76 and 77 of the Indic transcript, in light of the fact that the witness has said he read this transcript as part of his preparation for his report.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. So then, Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness into the courtroom again.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, I would draw your attention to the Indic transcript which you have before you, and I would ask you to turn to page 76, if that hasn't been done. You will see from this part of the transcript that the investigator, Barry Hogan, whose initials are BH, on the left-hand margin of this document, made reference to a tape recording from 29 May 1992. Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you see that the investigator asks Major Indic whether he's ever heard of this tape recording before?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Here it says "do you recognise the voice?" It doesn't ask about the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My first question is: Does it say that the witness Indic had heard of the tape and that he had heard parts of the tape prior to it being played to him on that day?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: This could be concluded from the first line.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Okay. Witness, have -- prior to reading the transcript of this interview with Major Indic, had you ever heard of this tape before? Had you heard of the tape? Not whether you heard the tape but whether you heard of it. Had you heard of the existence of this tape before you read this transcript?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard this tape and I saw it, because the Defence showed it to me. I heard it myself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall approximately when the first time that you heard this tape was?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I really don't, because this war lasted for over two years. I could confuse the issues. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you know approximately what year or month in which year you first heard this tape? Can you be any more specific whatsoever?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I can't. I really can't. I can't be specific. I apologise.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Did you ever hear at any point during the war in Bosnia, did you ever hear about the existence of this tape or the contents of this tape?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I never heard about it or saw it until the Defence provided me with the opportunity of seeing it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And did you listen to the tape or did you read a transcript of what the tape said or both?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did both.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: I would first like to have one clarification. One of your answers says that you had an opportunity seeing the tape, whereas I understand that we are talking about an audiotape. And your last answer was that you did hear the tape and read the transcript. I'm just confused.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreter's correction: The witness said "heard."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I had the opportunity of seeing a videotape of an event in the Sarajevo theatre. That was a videotape. But the Defence provided me with the transcript of this audiotape.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Which relates to this event.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: That clarifies the issue. I don't know whether the tape is about an event or not. But please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, you've told us that you both heard the tape and read the transcript. In your own mind, did you verify that the information contained in the transcript accurately reflected what you heard on the audiotape?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really didn't pay attention to that. When the Defence provided me with this, I -- well, I really am not in a position, I'm not capable of checking whether the tape corresponds to the text. That would require an entire investigation, and I didn't have the time nor the need for that. You have to follow a methodology in order to check the authenticity and the probative value of all the documents. I don't know how to do this. It wasn't necessary for me to do this because I thought that this had already been done in the course of previous proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, my question goes more to the accuracy of the transcripts. In other words, did you listen to the tape and then did you read the transcript and make a comparison between the accuracy of the transcript in comparison to what you heard on the audiotape?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't carry out any checks of any kind because I didn't think that that was an obligation of mine. And this is something I don't know how to do.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Well, witness, when you -- do you remember if you heard the tape first or if you read the transcript first?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really don't know. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall whether when you read the transcript anything occurred to you in reading that that you thought perhaps you hadn't heard that on the tape?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I didn't.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could I ask now that the witness be handed copies of the transcript of the tape.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, if you could please place the transcript that I have provided you on the ELMO so that we can all see what you're looking at. That would be helpful.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the benefit of the Chamber and the Defence, the witness I've attention is being drawn to the bottom of the third page of this document and similarly the third page of the English translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, Mr. President. I need to ask the Prosecution to clarify something. When we are told that this document is dated May 1992, why do we find on page -- there's no page number here -- ERN number 1065909 a date 31 July 1993? And I'm asking this in order to avoid any confusion. Could I be told what this is referring to, since the date itself is apparently a different date. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Could anyone, before we listen to, tell me what Bjelasnica is or -- I don't know how to pronounce it. Perhaps the interpreters could. The word B-j-e-l-a-s-n-i-c-a.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Bjelasnica, Mr. President. It is a hill, a mountain around Sarajevo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. A topographic -- yes. Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, the document that you have before you contains a number of translations from various intercepts. The one in question, as I've indicated, is the one on the bottom of the third page. The one that Mr. Piletta-Zanin is referring to has no relevance with respect to the questions being put to this witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, my question was: Why we have the dates for what isn't relevant and we don't have dates for what is relevant. And I'm referring to the transcript such as it has been typed out.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis, any response to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We have no response to that, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: So you say we have not in this document the date written down. So that's still -- other sources would have to provide for.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That's correct, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Could it be -- could the relevant parts be taken out from this document so that finally if you tender it, we limit ourselves to --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Absolutely, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: -- The part that is relevant, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, we're referring simply to the part beginning on the bottom of the third page and continuing to about halfway down the fourth page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. I am sorry, but since we are contesting the way in which these documents were established, I think it would be extremely useful - and this is an objection to the response of the Prosecution - it would be useful to show that if there are documents -- as if by accident there are documents for which there are dates and it's almost accidental -- it seems accidental that there are documents which we have dates. This seems important given the probative nature of the document if it should be submitted as evidence. And this is the issue to which I am objecting and I am objecting to the response.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: The Chamber will still have to consider, Mr. Mundis, whether we would like to -- this document to be split up, in view of the different data for different parts of this document. So we'll decide on that later. But Mr. Piletta-Zanin, the objection is denied, but I immediately add that the purpose for which these questions were permissible should be kept in mind. So that's the -- if we keep that in mind, then you may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Witness, again, turning to the part that you have before you, beginning at the bottom of the page next to the number "1" where it says "Mladic." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you please take a moment and read, beginning at "Mladic" through the following page where it ends at the word "goodbye."

utterances.speaker: RADOVAN RADINOVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Are you asking me whether I know how to read? I don't see why I should read this. This isn't a document I quoted. It's not part of my report. I didn't refer to it. Why should I read it?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Because you're asked to do so. Would you please read it, so that you can answer questions in relation to this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to read it aloud. It's just to make yourself acquainted with the content of this part of this text.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I am familiar with parts of the text now, but I am still against reading it. I'm not here to read. I've come here to answer questions. But if I have to read, I can do that too. But I don't think there is any sense in asking me to read something that is not mine.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Would you please read it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] "Mladic --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: You don't have to read it aloud. It is just for yourself, that you're acquainted with the text.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I've read it for myself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Then please proceed, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I take it -- do I take it from that comment by the Bench that we -- that the Chamber does not want him to read it out loud?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Oh, if there's any specific -- you didn't ask him to read it out aloud, so I thought that it would be just for the witness to, but --

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Objection, Mr. President. With regard to what you said, to the extent that it is a matter not of establishing the reality of an alleged conversation that General Mladic had but in the sense to test the procedure or the methodology used by General Radinovic. We don't see how the facts of reading it out aloud could change anything. So it's an objection that has to do with principles. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Piletta-Zanin, we discussed this issue in the absence of the witness. The decision was given on purpose in the absence of the witness. You should not have discussed the -- whereas I, when I referred to the purpose, I specifically did not refer to what that purpose was because it's not of any relevance for the witness. Could we just -- I'll read it to you, Mr. Radinovic, so that we know what the text is about. Mr. Mundis, you're talking about the part -- in the translation, exactly what part is it?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The part, Mr. President, beginning number 1: "Mladic," at the bottom of page 3, continuing to the middle of page 4.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before we continue, Mr. Piletta-Zanin -- reading out this text aloud, would this really -- would this really assist in reaching the purposes?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I -- I would ask to be heard on that point in the absence of the witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Perhaps we have to adjourn anyhow. General, we would continue tomorrow. It's about time to stop. And we still have to deal with this -- with this procedural issue. So I would like to see you back tomorrow morning at 9.00 in this same courtroom. And may I instruct you as I did before not to speak with anyone about the testimony you have given and you're about to give. Yes?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, that's clear.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Madam Usher, could you please escort the witness out of the courtroom.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, if I may, I'd like to address the Chamber in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. We'll turn into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: We're close to the conclusion of the Defence case, and there's still a few outstanding issues on exhibits. May I invite the parties to look carefully to -- to look to the testimony of Dusan Dunjic, Dr. Dusan Dunjic. The Chamber is asking to party to peruse the documents used during the testimony of this witness and also inviting the parties to decide which documents they wish to tender. And as far as my recollection goes, this has not yet been done. Then in respect of Witness DP35, if you'd look at the transcript of the 17th of January, I think, the parties are invited to produce the whole of the senior military observers end-of-the-month reports of December and of January. And if you look at the transcript, you'll see the Chamber requested the production of a certain set of documents. It's my recollection that it has not yet been done. But if I'm mistaken, I'd like to hear from the parties. Then the final issue is that in view of the Defence witness expert report, the procedure followed during the presentation of the Prosecution's case was that finally they have been formally tendered and admitted under P number. So therefore, the Defence is invited to tender the Defence expert reports in a similar way and to grant them D numbers. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. PILETTA-ZANIN
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. President, very briefly. With regard to the end-of-the-year reports, I think that we have done what we were supposed to do. They've already been provided to the registry. As far as the expert reports are concerned, we are assuming that given the absence of our usual registrar, who is familiar with this file, we will deal with it with the person who will be replacing the registrar tomorrow in order to avoid wasting time. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: As a matter of fact, it's not mainly whether these documents have been produced. Perhaps I expressed myself not in a correct way. But they have not been formally tendered, finally. And it could be done in several ways: One of the ways of doing it is giving it a C number and then the parties would know that these were Chamber exhibits, rather than party exhibits. Then I finally inform you that since these documents might take some time as well, there are some others that -- on which we still have to give decisions. If needed, the Chamber explores the possibility of getting some extra hours next Thursday. It's not sure that we could use them for several reasons, but this is to inform the parties that the Chamber envisages to, if needed, to gain some extra hours on Thursday afternoon. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning --

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: I'm sorry, just before you --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Before I adjourn, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: By "Thursday," do you mean Thursday this week or Thursday next week?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Thursday this week.

utterances.speaker: MR. IERACE
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Then -- Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sorry, Mr. President. If it would be possible, later this afternoon the Prosecution would appreciate an indication perhaps from the registrar as to how much time remains for cross-examination of this witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
utterances.text: Yes. Well, we usually deduce the time the witness has spent out of court, and that -- when I said that the remaining time would be approximately one hour, we started again at ten minutes to 1.00. Examination was interrupted a couple of times. And some 15 minutes were taken. So if that is some guidance, three hours and twenty would make approximately, I would say, four hours and perhaps 10, 15 minutes. But we have to make more precise calculations on that. We'll adjourn until tomorrow morning, 9.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ORIE
